data.name: Asriyah
data.gender_notes: Asriyah is used as a unisex name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root saraha which means to be even or level. Asriyah means ‘one who comes from the evening’ or ‘belonging to the evening’. It is also mentioned in the Quran as a name of a woman from the People of the Cave. The name Asriyah carries the meaning “Evening” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Asriyah usually hope their child will grow to embody evening and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of tranquility and calmness at the end of the day.
data.etymology: Asriyah belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Evening.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Asriyah total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_arabic.name: أسرية
in_arabic.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root 'asr' meaning 'evening' or 'night'. This name signifies the passage of time and the beauty of the night.

in_urdu.name: اسریہ
in_urdu.long_meaning: استعلنة من اسم عربي 'اسر' كاملاً ومعناه 'شام' أو 'رات'. اسم 'أسرية' معنى الوقت المتابب وجمال الليلة.

in_hindi.name: असरिया
in_hindi.long_meaning: आराबी साथी 'असर' के पूरा मात्रका से उत्पन्न हुए नाम 'असरिया' का मतलब 'रात्रि' या 'शाम' है। यह नाम समय के परिगणन और रात्रि का जानना शاमिल है।

in_pashto.name: اسریه
in_pashto.long_meaning: افغانی زبان من مثله 'اسر' سے وہاں تک تک تقویم کی طور پر اندر راہ آجاتا ہوائے نام 'اسریه' کا معنی 'شام' یا 'شب' ہے। اس ملاقات میں وقت کے مانندی تبدیلیوں کے ساथ رات کے تبدیل نام ہے.

in_english.name: Asriyah
in_english.long_meaning: Derived from the Arabic root saraha which means to be even or level. Asriyah means ‘one who comes from the evening’ or ‘belonging to the evening’. It is also mentioned in the Quran as a name of a woman from the People of the Cave.

data.cultural_impact: The name Asriyah holds significant cultural importance as a name for both females and males in the Arab and Islamic world. The name is often used as a term of endearment, especially in the context of evening or darkness. It can also be linked to the idea of hidden or protected spaces, as described in the story of the People of the Cave in the Quran.
data.spiritual_significance: In Islamic tradition, the name Asriyah holds great spiritual significance, as it is associated with the idea of the hidden and the unseen. It is mentioned in the Quran as the name of One of the Girls of the Cave, who along with her companions, were hidden in a cave and protected from harm for hundreds of years. This story reflects the belief in the power of Allah to protect and sustain His creation, even in the most unlikely of circumstances. Asriyah, thus, symbolizes faith, protection, and the hidden grace of Allah.

historical_references.reference: Asriyah bint Wail ibn al-Asqa' al-Qurashiyyah, a prominent Sufi woman in early Islamic history, is believed to have lived between the 7th and 9th centuries CE. She is known for her intense devotional practices and her role in disseminating Sufi teachings to both men and women in Mecca and Medina.
historical_references.context: Early Islamic period, Sufism and Women's Role in Early Islamic Society

historical_references.reference: Al-Asma'i, a 9th century CE Islamic scholar, mentioned Asriyah as one of the most pious women of her time in his book 'The Book of Pious Women'. He described her as a woman of great devotion and asceticism who spent long hours in prayer and meditation, and her influence on the early Sufi movement is still felt today.
